reason: A keeps one fixed phone card with a folder map. In every step a dot follows the path to where it really ends: three '..' climbing out to srv/archive, the shared-link jumping across to srv, tmp-other landing next to tmp. The core idea (text vs real destination) is visible, not just described, and that also makes A a natural GIF source. Its step 3 quiz (4 real test requests), step 5 sandbox (typed paths judged correctly by both gates, e.g. tmp2/x, shortcut-then-up to /srv/private.txt, cache/../stale.txt allowed) and step 6 dot scoreboard (14/14, 5/14, 0/14, 0/14 with 4/8, 0/14) are all correct. B is equally accurate and slightly more careful: it says outright that 5 of 14 is 'a list of tricks it misses, not a failure rate', explains why the other 9 were blocked and notes the assumed trusted approval. But B is a long scrolling text lesson. Its path walk highlights rows in an indented text tree that mostly runs below the fold, and its scoreboard tooltip covers rows. That makes B less visual, less stable on a phone and harder to turn into a GIF.

A: Step 5 gate reasons are cut off with an ellipsis ('ends at /workspace/acme/output/summary.txt, inside ...'), and the gate box and map labels are small (about 11-12 px) and dense on a 390 px phone.
The path-trace lines zigzag across folder labels on the map, making some walks (e.g. the step 4 climb-out) hard to follow at a glance.

It never explains that the other 9 forbidden requests were blocked only because they started outside the folder, so '5 of 14' could be read as a failure rate (only 'all five path tricks' and the step 7 ceiling note hint at this). Also, the 4/4 quiz answer drops its right/wrong verdict.
B: Two numbering systems clash: the 2/7 screen is labelled 'STEP 1', and the scoreboard refers to 'the 5 tricks from step 3', which is screen 4/7.
On the 6/7 scoreboard the sticky 'Tap a square' detail panel covers the Safer gate rows on first view. The step 4 trick chips are clipped at the right edge.
The step 4 'walk' is a highlight moving down a long text tree that runs below the fold, so the reader has to scroll during the animation. Screens scroll to 1,100-1,400 px, which suits a GIF poorly.
